cleared.check: Task 1 method. A driver (scripts/realrun.py in the work directory) regenerates script sets 1, 2 and 6 of tools/opdiff (pmdiff.py seed 7_2026_11_24, 250 scripts; pmdiff2.py seed 11_2026_11_24, 300 scripts; pmdiff6.py, 706 scripts) with every reference to the PoolManager pointed at the network's real PoolManager address from state/networks.json, and runs each as one eth_call at 25 million gas against 'latest'. The state override contains only the driver (unlock callback, which also pays native value from its own overridden balance in set 6), the token doubles at 0xc0ffee01, 0xc0ffee02 and 0xc0ffee05 and the hook doubles at 0x486b.... and 0x486c....; the PoolManager's code, storage and balance are left as on chain. Pools are created by the scripts with those currencies and hooks, so no existing pool is touched. For each network the code at the real address was fetched in the same run (24,009 bytes, 24,050 on Unichain). Records were compared call by call with Ethereum's record at Ethereum's real address after replacing the 20 bytes of each PoolManager address with a marker (scripts/compare.py, scripts/alldiffs.py), and with the fresh-address results stored in opcodes/pmdiff.json, pmdiff2.json and pmdiff6.json. Every script whose answer differed from the stored fresh answer was run again at the real address with 2,000,000,000, 150,000,000, 50,000,000 or 30,000,000 gas, the first the endpoint accepts (scripts/gasretry.py). Ethereum's fresh-address answers for sets 2 and 6 were rerun the same day for a call-by-call comparison.
cleared.result: At Ethereum's real address 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90 the 250 set 1 records and the 300 set 2 records are byte-identical to the stored fresh-address reference hashes, and the 706 set 6 records equal this cycle's Ethereum fresh-address rerun except where a script reads the PoolManager's own storage (owner, controller, accrued fees, extsload ranges) and in script 260, where the revert data of a native take to the PoolManager itself names the PoolManager's address; scripts 275 to 277 are byte-identical between the two addresses. So placing the scripts at the real address, with real code and storage, changes no amount, delta, slot or revert reason that does not come from the stored state itself.

cleared.check: Task 1, set 1 (pool math, 250 scripts, no hook and no token code) at the real PoolManager address of all 21 networks.
cleared.result: 18 networks return all 250 records byte-identical to Ethereum's real-address records after address masking. Polygon (231 equal), Monad (229) and Tempo (240) differ on exactly the script indexes that differed at the fresh address (opcodes/pmdiff.json), each first differing call a full-range swap that failed with empty return data on the network side at 25 million gas. With more gas 12 of Polygon's 19, 14 of Monad's 21 and 8 of Tempo's 10 become identical to the stored Ethereum hash; the rest still end in a gas-starved swap at the largest gas each endpoint accepts, as OPCODES.md already records. No set 1 record differs between the real address and the stored fresh-address result of the same network.

cleared.check: Task 1, set 2 (hook doubles, token double with nine transfer shapes, sync and settle against a moving balance, native payouts to an account without code and to precompiles 1 and 4) at the real address. In the fresh runs the PoolManager was given 10^19 wei by override; here it holds its real native balance.
cleared.result: 16 networks equal Ethereum on all 300. Elysium and HyperEVM differ on script 189 only and Polygon and Monad on the same 20 scripts as at the fresh address; each starts at a swap that failed with empty return data, and with more gas 189 becomes identical on Elysium and HyperEVM and 12 of 20 on Polygon and Monad. Tempo differs on 35: the six gas-limited ones it had at the fresh address (four become identical with more gas) and the 29 scripts with native payouts (index 9 mod 10), where every native take of 1 or 10^15 wei fails with WrappedError(recipient, 0, revert data, NativeTransferFailed) (selector 0x90bfb865) at the real address. Tempo has no native asset: eth_getBalance answers the constant 4242...42 for every account, and a value transfer from the real PoolManager fails, while the fresh run had a balance placed by override. A take of zero native and every ERC-20 take behave as on Ethereum. This is the PoolManager having no native balance, recorded already in cleared.json for Tempo, not a change in an amount the code computes.

cleared.check: Task 1, set 6 (706 scripts for the jump sides sets 1 to 5 missed) at the real address. At the fresh address pmdiff6 made the driver the owner (storage slot 0 override) and gave the PoolManager 10^19 wei; at the real address the owner, protocol fee controller, accrued protocol fees and native balance are each network's own. Every differing call was tested against the network's state read independently with eth_getStorageAt and eth_call (scripts/explain.py): a call counts as explained when both sides succeeded with equal length and each differing word is the network's value of the same state item whose Ethereum value appears on the Ethereum side.
cleared.result: On every network the only set 6 scripts that differ from Ethereum's real-address record are: 246, 662, 671, 696 (reads of owner(), slot 0 through delegatecall, short calldata and callback paths: the word is the network's owner, slot 0, equal to the owner in networks.json); 672 (protocolFeeController(), slot 2); 641 to 643, 673, 676, 685 (protocolFeesAccrued(address(0)) words, and owner-only or controller-only calls that revert with UNAUTHORIZED or InvalidCaller because the driver is not the owner); 698 to 702 (extsload(0, n) and extsload(2^256-2, n), whose slot counter wraps to slot 0 in Extsload.sol:34, so they return slot 0 and slot 2); 657 on Base only (balanceOf(address(0), 0) returns 45,056,898,864, a native ERC-6909 claim balance that someone minted to address(0) on Base, read at several blocks back to 61,054,597 with the same value, 0 on the other 20 networks); 239, 241, 248 to 260 (native payouts that need more native than the real PoolManager holds: Zora 0.152, World Chain 5.42, MegaETH 1.997 and HyperEVM 11.35 units against takes of 10^18 to 2*10^19+1 wei, Tempo none); 275 to 277 and 279 (an initialize at the price limits followed by swaps that run out of the 25 million gas on every network, Ethereum included, and become identical to the stored reference with more gas, the reference interpreter rerun of script 275 confirming the stored hash); 681 and 682 on Monad, Polygon and BNB Chain (currency 0x1000, a system contract or the staking precompile there, as recorded in cycle 12). All other words are equal on all 21 networks, so the 690 or so remaining scripts per network give the same amounts, deltas, slots and revert data at the real address as at Ethereum's.

cleared.check: Address-keyed rules that the fresh-address runs could not meet (lead L-810): Arc's check on every call that carries value (F-125), Avalanche's fold of bit 248 of storage indexes onto existing slots (F-040), Tempo's transfer policies, MegaETH's per-account accounting, and any compile or cache decision keyed by address, code hash or use count.
cleared.result: Arc: all native payouts of sets 2 and 6 from the real PoolManager (to an account without code, to precompiles 1 and 4, to the driver, to hooks that revert) give Ethereum's words; the real PoolManager is not refused as a sender. Avalanche: all 1,256 scripts give Ethereum's words while the real PoolManager has its real storage, so no slot the scripts write or read is folded onto an existing PoolManager slot. MegaETH: the only differences are the native balance cases; no per-account gas rule changed a result at 25 million gas. Tempo: no difference outside native value; the token doubles are not TIP-20 tokens, so Tempo's TIP-403 transfer policies were not exercised by these sets. Monad: eth_call always interprets (F-130), so the hotness-keyed compiler is not reachable by this method, and the compiled code of the deployed PoolManager was compared with the interpreter in cycles 15 and 16. Every client named in OPCODES.md as keeping a code or jump cache keys it by content, and the real address runs are consistent with that.

cleared.check: Task 2 (lead L-802). cycles/016/arbitrum-family.work/scripts/offsets.py, copied to scripts/offsets.py with the network list taken from the command line and execution errors no longer retried, was run on the 18 networks where it had not run: 200 vectors per network, CALLDATALOAD, CALLDATACOPY with length 64 and 0, CODECOPY, KECCAK256 of length 0, MCOPY of length 0, and RETURNDATACOPY of 8 and 0 bytes after a 40 byte return, each with 25 offsets from 0 through 2^31, 2^32, 2^63, 2^64, 2^128 and 2^256-1.
cleared.result: 3600 vectors, 0 mismatches. Every word equals the specification and the word the three Arbitrum chains returned in cycle 16 (3,600 of 3,600 equal to Arbitrum One's). On every network the same 43 vectors fail, exactly the return data copies the specification makes an exceptional halt (offset plus length above 40, including the wrapped 2^256-1 + 8), and nothing else fails: zero-length copies and hashes at offsets up to 2^256-1 succeed without memory expansion. The failure messages differ by client and not in outcome: 'EVM error: OutOfOffset' on the reth based nodes, 'return data out of bounds' on bor, BNB Chain geth, Avalanche and Celo's op-geth backend (7 of Celo's 43 came from that backend, 36 from reth), 'revert: OutOfOffset' on Arc, and 'out of gas' on Monad. Monad reporting the halt as out of gas does not change what the PoolManager sees, because a failed frame returns 0 to its caller either way and the PoolManager copies return data only up to RETURNDATASIZE (src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-160).

cleared.check: Task 3. At the real address of each network, scripts/tslots.py read IS_UNLOCKED_SLOT (Lock.sol:8), NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT_SLOT (NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:8-9), RESERVES_OF_SLOT and CURRENCY_SLOT (CurrencyReserves.sol:11,13, each recomputed as keccak256 of its name minus 1) and the delta slots of the driver for three currencies: (A) by a plain eth_call of exttload(bytes32[]) at 'latest' and 'pending' from address 0, 0xdead and the driver; (B) in one simulated call with only the driver overridden: before unlock, first thing inside the callback, after sync of a token double holding 1000, after mint(driver, id, 5), after burn of the same, and after unlock returned; (C) the same four constants and slots 0 and 1 through extsload, as persistent slots.
cleared.result: 21 of 21 networks pass all three. A: all seven words are 0 in all six calls, so no unlock flag, delta count, synced currency, reserve or delta from an earlier transaction of the block is visible to a simulated call. B: before unlock 0,0,0,0; inside the callback unlocked 1 and the rest 0; after sync the currency and 1000; count 1 and delta -5 after mint, count 0 and delta 0 after burn; after unlock the flag is 0 and the count 0, while the synced currency and reserves stay set, which is what the source writes (sync is cleared only by settle, CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36, PoolManager.sol:279-288). C: the four constants read 0 as persistent slots, so no client mixes the transient and persistent spaces at these indexes.

cleared.check: Base, ERC-6909 claims held by address(0). balanceOf(address(0), 0) on the real PoolManager returns 45,056,898,864 (about 4.5e-8 ETH of native claims).
cleared.result: This is existing state, not an interpreter effect: the value is the same at blocks 61,054,597 to 62,054,600 on two endpoints. mint accepts any recipient (PoolManager.sol:322-329, ERC6909.sol:79-83), so somebody minted claims to address(0) and paid for them; those claims can never be burned or moved, because burn and transferFrom need msg.sender to be address(0) or approved by it (ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22, ERC6909.sol:35-48). The native backing stays in the PoolManager as surplus. No other user loses anything.

cleared.check: Monad reports a RETURNDATACOPY past the end of return data as 'out of gas' (JSON-RPC code -32603), where the specification and the other clients name it an out-of-bounds halt.
cleared.result: Both are exceptional halts that consume the frame's gas and return failure to the caller, and the vector's outcome equals the specification. The PoolManager never copies return data beyond RETURNDATASIZE (Hooks.callHook and CustomRevert.bubbleUpAndRevertWith use returndatasize as the length), so the label cannot change a result of the bytecode. Only an off-chain tool that parses the error text would see it.

leads.question: Run set 2 at Tempo's real PoolManager address with a real TIP-20 token (for example pathUSD) as currency1 instead of the token double, with balances placed on the token's own storage, so that Tempo's TIP-403 transfer policy checks run against the real PoolManager address. Do take, sync and settle give the words they give with the double?
leads.why: The token doubles of sets 2 and 6 are ordinary contracts, so the address-keyed transfer policy of Tempo's token precompile was not exercised by this unit; a policy that treated the PoolManager address specially would freeze every pool that holds that token (A6).

leadResults.answer: Sets 1, 2 and 6 (1,256 scripts) were run at the real PoolManager address of all 21 networks with code and storage as on chain and only the driver, token doubles and hook doubles injected. Ethereum at its real address equals the stored fresh results for sets 1 and 2 byte for byte. Every other difference is explained: the PoolManager's own owner, controller, accrued protocol fees and, on Base, claims minted to address(0), read through owner(), protocolFeeController(), protocolFeesAccrued, extsload ranges that wrap to slot 0 and balanceOf; native payouts larger than the real native balance on Zora, World Chain, MegaETH, HyperEVM and Tempo; swaps that run out of gas at 25 million, the same scripts as at the fresh address; and currency 0x1000 on Polygon, BNB Chain and Monad. No network answers with a different amount, delta, slot or revert reason at its real address.

offsets.py ran on the 18 networks it had not reached: 3,600 vectors, no mismatch, every word equal to the Arbitrum chains' and the specification's, and the same 43 specified halts on every network. The Go clients (bor v2.11.1, BNB Chain geth v1.8.2, avalanchego 1.15.3, Celo's op-geth backend) and Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc and HyperEVM give the specified result; only the error text differs (Monad calls the out-of-bounds halt 'out of gas').
